title.narrative: Rakhine: Humanitarian support for children and their families through Education and Food Security interventions

description.narrative: ltpgtSave the Children International (SCI) will deliver a 12-month multi-sectoral project to meaningfully contribute to the wellbeing of affected children, their families, and communities. This project includes interventions in education and food security to support 8,385 beneficiaries (1,914 women, 2,655 girls, 1,469 men and 2,347 boys) SCI is committed to improving education in IDP camps by increasing access and quality in a safe and inclusive manner. SCI will establish or rebuild temporary learning spaces (TLSs) in IDP camps in Sittwe, with gender-segregated and disability-inclusive latrines in IDP the camps, providing a conducive environment for children's education. To support educational improvements, SCI aims to involve the local community by establishing or continuing Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs). Essential materials for teaching and learning will be supplied to both students and educators. SCI also prioritizes inclusive education and will provide teachers with training in creating inclusive learning environments, including topics, such as, gender sensitivity, mental health support, and disability-inclusion practices. Teachers will also receive orientation on Child Safeguarding (CSG) to ensure the safety and protection of children, including topics like Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and Psychological and Social Support (PSS).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSCI will support food security for affected households in Sittwe and Pauktaw through Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), which aims to meet the immediate basic needs of targeted individuals in IDP camps and host communities. MPCA, while established in the value of SMEB for two months, will help restore immediate food security of households, but also contribute to partial livelihoods restoration of agricultural and fishery-based households in both camps and villages. This will contribute to the continuation of localized food production. Due to budget limitations this might not cover the full scope of losses suffered by the households but will provide at least partial support to those struggling to continue with their productive engagement. The target population will be identified on vulnerability basis taking into account damages suffered during the cyclone. This approach aligns with the recommendations of the Food Security cluster. The amount of MPCA provided for each household will follow the recommendations of the Cash Working Group, which will provide a two-month SMEB amount. SCI will follow the Food Security Cluster’s recommendations and distribute cash in line with recommendations of the Cash Working Group.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSpecific needs of persons with disabilities, the elderly, women, girls, boys are considered in the proposal and provision/scope of assistance. This will include prioritization of women headed households for MPCA support, as well as inclusion of household financial decision-making messages during the distributions. Wherever possible, SCI will provide MPCA to PwD in an amount based on local assessment, especially in cases where this can lead to self-sufficiency and productive engagement of PwD. SCI will prioritize the Centrality of Protection by its commitments to PSEA and Accountability to Affected People (AAP) throughout the implementation. Community and child-friendly Information Education Communication (IEC) tools on explosive ordnance risks will also be rolled out, where appropriate, to promote awareness among the communities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
